symbols.name: first sequence
symbols.meaning: The first of the two sequences whose cyclic convolution is taken, with entries a_0 through a_{q-1}.
symbols.quote: Let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{q-1})$ and $b = (b_0, \dots, b_{q-1})$ be two sequences, where $q$ is the number of entries in each sequence.

symbols.name: second sequence
symbols.meaning: The second of the two sequences whose cyclic convolution is taken, with entries b_0 through b_{q-1}.
symbols.quote: Let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{q-1})$ and $b = (b_0, \dots, b_{q-1})$ be two sequences, where $q$ is the number of entries in each sequence.

symbols.name: sequence length
symbols.meaning: The number of entries in each of the sequences a and b, which is also the length of their cyclic convolution.
symbols.quote: Let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{q-1})$ and $b = (b_0, \dots, b_{q-1})$ be two sequences, where $q$ is the number of entries in each sequence.

symbols.name: cyclic convolution
symbols.meaning: The sequence a \ast b of the same length q, whose entries are the cyclic convolution sums c_o.

symbols.name: output index
symbols.meaning: The index of an entry of the cyclic convolution c, running from 0 to q-1.
symbols.quote: where $o$ indexes the output entries and $i$ indexes the terms of the sum; here $i$ changes meaning from its use for digit indices on earlier pages.

symbols.name: summation index
symbols.meaning: The index of the terms of the sum for c_o, running from 0 to q-1; it replaces its earlier meaning as a digit index.
symbols.quote: where $o$ indexes the output entries and $i$ indexes the terms of the sum; here $i$ changes meaning from its use for digit indices on earlier pages.
